Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  August 7, 2025

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council Chambers
located on the ninth floor of City Hall on August 7, 2025. Commissioner Denmon called the meeting
to order at 6:00 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Cynthia McLemore
  - District 3, Commissioner Christopher Beck - District 4
  Absent:  Commissioner Octavio Padilla - District 2, Commissioner Henry Brown -
  Commissioner at Large

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Thomas Uwal  Director of Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Anthony Harris  Recreation Supervisor
  Geoffrey Okamoto  Human Services Transportation Manager
  Gilbert Gonzalez  Graffiti Abatement Supervisor
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner McLemore and seconded by Commissioner Beck that
the minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on June 5, 2025, be approved.
The following roll call vote carried the motion:

Ayes: Commissioners McLemore, Beck and Denmon
Noes: None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORT - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Park Maintenance Supervisor, Gilbert Gonzalez reported the
following: Parks Division - The Manchester median beautification project is continuing. Flagstones
have been placed in the western end of the median and four crape myrtle trees arrived today and
will soon be planted in the median. After the trees are planted, seasonal flowers will be added to
the planters. Graffiti Division - In July, staff experienced heavy activity in the following areas:
District 4: in alleys on Crenshaw between Century and Imperial Highway, Imperial Highway
between Yukon and Simms and Darby Dixon and Bartdon Ave. Tree Division - The City’s tree
contractor, West Coast Arborists, just completed planting 85 trees throughout the City and are
finishing their annual palm trimming. The Graffiti hotline is (310) 412-8739.

REPORT - RECREATION. Recreation Supervisor, Anthony Harris reported the following: Youth
sports- The City of Inglewood citywide youth sports division continues their year round sports

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

offerings with the summer Dodgers Dreamteam season. The league offers 22 teams, assembled
over 5 age divisions, with 26 coaches, and 296 players. The season culminates on August 30th with
Championship Saturday were all division winners will be crowned and team parties will be
executed. All participants will walk away with a positive experience, season awards, and a meal to
conclude the season. Shout out to all the volunteer coaches, field champions, and sports staff that
work extremely hard to create positive memories for the youth of the community. Next up,
Inglewood Rams flag football season in the fall of 2025. Movies in the Park- I want to invite all of
you to join us for the final showing of our Movies in the Park series this summer. This event will
occur on Saturday, August 16th, at North Park, featuring Despicable Me 4, the last movie in this
year’s series. All movies are free and begin at dusk. Food and refreshments will be available for
purchase. We encourage you to bring your blankets and lawn chairs and enjoy an unforgettable
evening of cinema under the stars. It’s truly been a wonderful summer. Each movie in the Park
series screening has drawn more than 300 attendees, creating a vibrant and engaging atmosphere
for families and community members. We have been fortunate to enjoy beautiful weather and a
strong sense of community at each event. We hope to see you there for a memorable closing
night! Early Learners Program Open House - The Early Learners Program is hosting an Open House
on Saturday, August 16th, from 10:30 – 11:30 a.m. at all three locations: Rogers Park, Siminski Park,
and Lockhaven Community Center. This is an excellent opportunity for families to explore
classrooms, meet the dedicated teachers and staff, and learn more about the enrollment process.
Siminski and Lockhaven offer classes for early learners ages 3-5 that focus on TK and Kinder
readiness. Rogers Park offers a Spanish Immersion class for students ages 3-5, a Tiny Tots class for
2 year olds that are potty-trained and a Parent & Me class for young learners ages 12 – 29 months.
Please share with friends and family who have little ones. All are invited and welcomed! Hispanic
Heritage Festival - This year’s annual Hispanic Heritage Festival will take place on Saturday,
September 20, from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Market Street in downtown Inglewood. There will be live
entertainment, a classic car show, information and vendor booths, health screenings, arts and
crafts, face painting, and a food court cooking up delicious and authentic food. The festival is FREE
and open to the public. Don’t forget to mark your calendars and save the date for this exciting
event. For more information on our Inglewood Youth Sports Leagues, visit our city sports website
at: https://cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com/

REPORT - HUMAN SERVICES. Human Services Transportation Operations Manager, Geoffrey
Okamoto reported on the following: Senior Nutrition - The Senior Center serves approximately
460 seniors per week through home-delivered meals for homebound seniors and congregate
meals. We continue to offer fresh produce weekly in partnership with the Social Justice Learning
Institute, and monthly shelf-stable meal boxes in collaboration with the Los Angeles Food Bank.
Farmers Market cards have been distributed, and seniors have been able to go on several trips to
the market from the center through our transportation services. Our numbers continue to climb
weekly in program participation, and we look forward to serving all of our seniors. Senior Center
Operations - Our Senior Center is experiencing significant growth, with notable increases in
participations numbers and an expanded range of programs. Mercedes Aguirre of the LA County
Department of Mental Health will be conducting a presentation on Discover your passion on
August 18. H.E.L.P (Helping Elderly Live Productively) will be conducting a presentation on Brain
Health on August 8.

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

CalFresh will be presenting a Wise Dining presentation on August 4 and August 25.On August 14,
we will screen the movie “The Greatest Game Ever Played" and host a Dance from 2:00 p.m. to
4:00 p.m. on August 28.On August 14 and August 27 we will be taking seniors to Redondo Beach
to enjoy an afternoon from 11:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. On August 13 will be doing a Luau celebration
from 10:00 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. (games, raffles). On August 20 we will be taking seniors to the LA
Zoo. Senior Center – Paratransit - The City of Inglewood’s paratransit program continues to
provide trips to seniors and the disabled community in Inglewood and Hawthorne. Our service is
currently seeking a full-time and part-time bus operator position in which we look forward to
having filled. We continue to strive in providing outstanding paratransit service to our community.

REPORT - DIRECTOR. Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department Director, Thomas
Uwal reported on the following: Inglewood Independence Day Music Festival - On Saturday, July
5, 2025, the City of Inglewood hosted its annual Independence Day Music Festival at the scenic
Darby Park, located at 3400 Arbor Vitae Street, Inglewood, CA 90305. Sponsored by Councilwoman
Faulk, the event celebrated community spirit and cultural diversity through a vibrant showcase of
live performances spanning R&B, Old-School Rock, Latin, Jazz, and Hip-Hop. Attendees enjoyed a
festive atmosphere featuring a diverse selection of food and merchandise vendors offering
multicultural cuisine, handmade jewelry, unique apparel, home décor, and refreshments.
Inglewood Family Unity Day - The 2nd Annual Family Unity Day, organized by District 1
Councilwoman Gloria Gray, took place on Saturday, July 26, 2025, at Darby Park. The event
welcomed families and community members for a day of togetherness, featuring live music,
cultural cuisine, and opportunities for community connection. Attendees brought picnic blankets
and lawn chairs to enjoy a relaxed, family-friendly atmosphere. The event fostered
intergenerational engagement, celebrated local talent, and strengthened relationships among
neighbors, civic leaders, and residents. Inglewood Pickleball Community Meeting -
On July 7, 2025, the City of Inglewood hosted a Pickleball Community Meeting at 6:00 PM in City
Hall's Community Room A. The meeting was attended by numerous local pickleball players, city
staff, Mayor James T. Butts, and Councilwoman Gloria Gray. The session focused on proposed
upgrades to pickleball courts and program improvements. Community members actively
participated in the discussion, sharing valuable input and feedback. The meeting proved to be
highly engaging and informative. FY 2025–2026 Budget Submission - As part of the City’s annual
budget planning process, all departments have submitted funding requests for Fiscal Year 2025–
2026. Our department presented a detailed budget proposal outlining projected revenues,
planned expenditures, program initiatives, and policy priorities. This document serves as a strategic
guide for resource allocation aimed at achieving departmental goals and supporting community-
focused services. The new fiscal year begins on October 1, 2025.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. None.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the meeting
adjourned at the hour of 6:39 p.m.
